## Purpose


1. Added a new NGram GPU speculator.
The main feature is a new implementation at: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/ngram/speculator.py`, similiar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29184.

2. Updated request state storage for NGram GPU.
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`
This changes how RequestState is initialized so that all_token_ids can stay densely resident on GPU instead of defaulting to UVA when ngram_gpu is active. As discussed in   #29184, the new n-gram speculator repeatedly scans active request token history, doing that from GPU-resident dense storage is much more appropriate than pulling through UVA-backed memory, this is a performance-oriented architectural change supporting the new feature.
The `model_runner.py` also injects req_states into speculators that need direct access to the persistent token store.

3. Added variable-length draft token plumbing
Several files were updated to support draft proposals where different requests may have different numbers of valid draft tokens:
`vllm/v1/outputs.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`
`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`

DraftTokenIds now includes:
`num_valid_draft_tokens: list[int] | None`.
Scheduler logic now truncates speculative tokens based on `num_valid_draft_tokens`.
`EngineCore adds _maybe_update_async_draft_token_ids()` to consume draft metadata from async execution and update scheduler state at the right time.



## Test Plan

```

--port 8000 \
--backend vllm \

Please file an issue. Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [...] Terminating request. Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The identical workload without speculative decoding succeeds 24/24. This was also reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. ## Environment ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.15.0 xgrammar: 0.2.3 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Maximum model length: 768 Maximum sequences: 16 Maximum batched tokens: 768 ``` Only one L40S GPU is required. ## Reproduction script The complete standalone reproduction script is attached as: [repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143661/repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py) The script does not depend on an external test framework. It automatically: 1. Starts vLLM with `ngram_gpu` and `xgrammar`. 2. Sends one structured request. 3. Sends 24 structured requests at concurrency 8. 4. Records the HTTP responses and relevant server errors. 5. Confirms that the server remains healthy. 6. Stops the server. 7. Starts an otherwise identical server without speculative decoding. 8. Repeats the same single and concurrent requests. 9. Writes all results to `result.json`. Run it with: ```bash python repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py \ --gpu 0 \ --out-dir ngram_gpu_xgrammar_repro ``` A `bug_reproduced` result intentionally exits with status 1. ## Failing server configuration The failing phase starts the server with: ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 768 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 \ --disable-log-stats \ --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram_gpu","num_speculative_tokens":4,"prompt_lookup_min":1,"prompt_lookup_max":4}' ``` ## JSON schema Every request uses the following schema: ```json { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } ``` ## Request input For request index `N`, the prompt is constructed as: ```python prefix = ( "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. " "Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. " ) * 6 prompt = ( f"{prefix}\nRequest id {N}. Return a JSON object with " '"status":"ok", "items":[1,2,3], and "request_id":' f"{N}." ) ``` The complete OpenAI-compatible request is: ```json { "model": "veritas-model", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. [repeated six times]\nRequest id 0. Return a JSON object with \"status\":\"ok\", \"items\":[1,2,3], and \"request_id\":0." } ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 80, "stream": false, "structured_outputs": { "json": { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } } } ``` ## Single-request result Before applying concurrent load, the script sends one request. Observed response: ```text HTTP 200 ``` The returned content is valid and satisfies the schema: ```json { "status": "ok", "items": [1, 2, 3], "request_id": 0 } ``` This confirms that: - The model is loaded correctly. - The request format is valid. - The schema is accepted. - xgrammar can compile and enforce the schema. - `ngram_gpu` can complete at least one structured request. ## Concurrent-load result The script sends: ```text Request count: 24 Concurrency: 8 ``` Observed result with vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Successful valid JSON responses: 3 HTTP 500 responses: 21 Invalid HTTP 200 responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Timeouts: 0 ``` The failed requests return: ```json { "error": { "code": 500, "message": "Internal server error", "param": null, "type": "InternalServerError" } } ``` ## Server log errors Representative server log output: ```text ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request ... for tokens 151667. Please file an issue. ``` ```text ERROR [scheduler.py:1835] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [151667] for request ... Terminating request. ``` Other rejected token IDs observed in the same run include: ```text 22335 630 ``` The API server subsequently reports: ```text Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The following log markers were all present: ```json { "failed_to_advance_fsm": true, "please_file_issue": true, "grammar_rejected_tokens": true, "internal_generation_error": true } ``` ## Server health after the failures After the 21 HTTP 500 responses, the script calls: ```text GET /v1/models ``` Observed result: ```text HTTP 200 ``` Therefore, this is a per-request internal generation failure rather than a complete server crash. ## Control without speculative decoding The script stops the failing server and starts an otherwise identical server without: ```text --speculative-config ``` The following settings remain unchanged: ```text Model Model dtype xgrammar backend JSON schema Prompts Request count Concurrency Maximum model length Maximum sequences Maximum batched tokens GPU ``` Control result: ```text Single request: HTTP 200, valid JSON Concurrent successful responses: 24 Concurrent HTTP 500 responses: 0 Invalid JSON responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` This isolates the failure to the interaction involving `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding. ## Reproduction on vLLM 0.26.0 The same interaction was previously reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. One run produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 ``` A separate run with asynchronous scheduling produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 2 HTTP 200, 22 HTTP 500 ``` The same server-side FSM and rejected-token errors were observed. The failure therefore reproduces on both: ```text vLLM 0.26.0 vLLM 0.27.1 ``` ## Expected behavior All valid concurrent structured-output requests should complete successfully. Speculative decoding may change performance, but it should not cause xgrammar to reject tokens that have already been accepted or committed by the scheduler. Expected result: ```text 24 HTTP 200 responses 24 valid JSON outputs 0 HTTP 500 responses ``` ## Actual behavior With `ngram_gpu` enabled: ```text 3 HTTP 200 responses 21 HTTP 500 responses ``` The structured-output FSM rejects generated tokens, the affected requests are terminated, and clients receive an internal server error. ## Reproducibility summary | Configuration | Single request | Concurrent result | Server after test | |---|---:|---:|---:| | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar without speculative decoding | Pass | 24/24 pass | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu, separate scheduling run | Pass | 2/24 pass, 22 HTTP 500 | Healthy | ## Attached evidence [result.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143667/result.json) [ngram_gpu_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143672/ngram_gpu_stdout.log) [ngram_gpu_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143685/ngram_gpu_stderr.log) [no_spec_control_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143690/no_spec_control_stdout.log) [no_spec_control_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143699/no_spec_control_stderr.log) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: ngram speculative decoding corrupts qwen3_coder tool-call parser output (empty/mangled arguments) for Qwen3.x models
items.body:
## Your current environment

```
vLLM version: 0.28.0
Image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
GPU: 1x NVIDIA H100 PCIe (single-GPU deployment, --tensor-parallel-size 1)
Models tested: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8
```

## 🐛 Describe the bug

When `--speculative-config` with `method: "ngram"` is enabled alongside `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` (also reproduces with the `qwen3_xml`/`mimo` aliases, which resolve to the same `Qwen3EngineToolParser` class) and `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, tool calls frequently come back with **empty or corrupted arguments**, despite the model's own reasoning trace showing it correctly decided on the right arguments.

Symptoms observed:
- `tool_calls[0].function.arguments == "{}"` (empty, argument silently dropped)
- Mangled keys, e.g. `{"command=ls": ""}` or `{"command=git status": ""}` — the argument value gets folded into the JSON key with an empty value
- In one case the function *name* itself was corrupted: `"runshell command=\"ls\""`
- Occasionally a raw XML tag leaks into the arguments string (e.g. a stray `</command>`)

**This is not a model capability issue.** I checked the `reasoning` field on every observed failure and in 12/12 sampled cases the model had already correctly decided on the exact right command (`ls`, `pwd`, `git status`, `ps aux`) before the tool call was emitted — the parser is dropping/corrupting an argument the model already produced correctly.

### Reproduction

Launch command (broken):
```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --quantization fp8 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "prompt_lookup_max": 4, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
```

Request:
```json
{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
  "max_tokens": 1000,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "List the files in the current directory using a shell command."}],
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "run_shell_command",
      "description": "Run a shell command and return its output",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"command": {"type": "string", "description": "The shell command to run"}},
        "required": ["command"]
      }
    }
  }],
  "tool_choice": "auto"
}
```

### Isolating the cause: removing `--speculative-config` fixes it completely

I ran a controlled 2×2 matrix (`enable_thinking` true/false × `temperature` 0.0/1.0, 5 prompts × 3 reps = 15 requests per cell, 60 requests total) with and without the `--speculative-config` flag, everything else identical.

**With `ngram` speculative decoding (broken):**

| Model | temperature=1.0 | temperature=0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B | 6/15 (40%) | 12/15 (80%) |
| Qwen3.6-27B (bf16 + `--quantization fp8`) | 5/15 (33%) | 3/15 (20%) |
| Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (native fp8 checkpoint) | 7/15 (47%) | 3/15 (20%) |
| Qwen3.8-27B, `enable_thinking=false` | 0/15 (0%) | 0/15 (0%) |

**Without `--speculative-config` at all (fixed), Qwen3.8-27B:**

| | temperature=0.0 | temperature=1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_thinking=true` | 15/15 (100%) | 15/15 (100%) |
| `enable_thinking=false` | 15/15 (100%) | 15/15 (100%) |

Removing only the `--speculative-config` flag (nothing else changed) took every cell from 0-80% to a clean 100%. This isolates ngram speculative decoding — not the model, not the reasoning/thinking interaction, not temperature — as the root cause.

I did **not** test whether other speculative methods (`mtp`, `eagle`, etc.) have the same issue — only `ngram` was implicated in this reproduction.

### Possible related issues

This looks like it could share a root cause with:
- #43221 — streaming reasoning tokens truncated when `</think>` and `<tool_call>` land in the same delta (my hypothesis: a multi-token speculative decode step is causing the parser to lose track of the boundary between reasoning content and the tool-call segment)
- #42021 — Qwen3.5 reasoning-parser/tool-call-parser conflict when thinking is enabled. Note: **the workaround suggested there (`chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`) did NOT help in my reproduction** — with `ngram` spec-decode still active, disabling thinking made things worse (0/30), and turned out to be a red herring: the real variable was speculative decoding, not thinking mode (see matrix above, where `enable_thinking=false` also hits 100% once spec-decode is removed).
- #22975, #29192, #30439 — related Qwen-coder tool-call parsing failures, none an exact match for this speculative-decoding-specific mechanism as far as I can tell.

### How you are running vLLM

Docker (`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`), docker-compose, single GPU pinned via `device_ids`.

items.title: [Feature]: Support combining multiple speculative decoding methods (e.g. MTP + ngram)
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Currently --speculative-config accepts a single method. It would be very useful to allow combining multiple speculative decoding methods in a single serving session — specifically, pairing a primary spec method (mtp, draft_model, EAGLE3, DFlash, etc.) with ngram as a secondary layer.
The motivation is that these methods are complementary by nature:

MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash, draft_model significantly accelerate the base generation speed by drafting semantically coherent tokens, but they provide little benefit on highly repetitive output — structured JSON, tool calls, code boilerplate, repeated schema tokens, etc.
ngram is effectively free (zero inference cost, no VRAM overhead) and excels precisely in those repetitive ranges, but contributes nothing to base generation speed on its own.

Running them together — the primary method drafting the semantically dense portion, ngram extending the tail in repetitive ranges — would make the two additive rather than redundant, capturing wins from both systems in a single verification pass.

### Alternatives

_No response_

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: Ngram speculative decoding produces corrupted output on hybrid GDN (Qwen3.5) models
items.body: ### Your current environment - vLLM version: `0.18.1rc1.dev43+gdebd6e768` (also reproducible on latest nightly `0.18.1rc1.dev236`) - GPU: NVIDIA GH200 480GB - Model: Qwen3.5-9b (Qwen3.5 architecture, `model_type: qwen3_5_text`, hybrid GDN + full attention) ### Model description Qwen3.5-based model with hybrid architecture: 24 GatedDeltaNet (linear attention) layers + 8 full attention layers. FP8 quantized via compressed-tensors. Config includes `layer_types: [linear_attention, linear_attention, linear_attention, full_attention, ...]` repeating pattern. ### How to reproduce the error **Without ngram (correct output):** ```bash # Start vLLM with no speculative decoding vllm serve model-fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \ --additional-config '{"gdn_prefill_backend": "triton"}' # Test curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "model-fp8", "prompt": "\nclass Calculator:\n def add(self, a, b):\n return a + b\n\n\nAdd subtract and multiply methods\n", "max_tokens": 300, "temperature": 0 }' ``` Output (correct): ``` class Calculator: def add(self, a, b): return a + b def subtract(self, a, b): return a - b def multiply(self, a, b): return a * b ``` **With ngram (corrupted output):** ```bash vllm serve model-fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 \ --additional-config '{"gdn_prefill_backend": "triton"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 64, "prompt_lookup_max": 10, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}' ``` Same prompt produces degenerate output with repeated fragments: ``` class Calculator: def add(self, a, b): return a + b def add(self, a, b): return a + b add(self, a, b): return a + b , a, b): return a + b ... ``` ### Relevant logs or traceback No crash or error — the model runs but produces corrupted output. The corruption pattern shows repeated/truncated fragments that degrade progressively, suggesting SSM state corruption rather than a sampling issue. ### Root cause analysis We traced this to how `mamba_utils.postprocess_mamba` handles token rejection during ngram speculative decoding on hybrid GDN models. **The problem** (`vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`, lines ~242-243): When ngram proposes N speculative tokens and some are rejected: 1. The **forward pass runs on all N proposed tokens**, advancing GDN SSM state by N steps 2. The rejection sampler correctly identifies which tokens were accepted (e.g., 2 of 4) 3. `postprocess_mamba` computes `num_tokens_running_state` and `new_num_computed_tokens` to determine which SSM state block to copy: ```python num_tokens_running_state = ( num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens - num_draft_tokens ) new_num_computed_tokens = num_tokens_running_state + num_accepted_tokens - 1 ``` 4. **But the SSM state was already evolved for all N tokens during the forward pass.** There is no mechanism to rollback/revert the GDN state to the position after only the accepted tokens. The state copy uses `accept_token_bias` to select which intermediate state to preserve, but this relies on the block-aligned state checkpoints being correct — which they aren't, because the SSM kernel (fused_recurrent) wrote states for all N tokens into contiguous block slots. **Why MTP doesn't have this issue:** MTP draft tokens are generated *after* the base model step completes, so the SSM state evolution and draft proposal are decoupled. With ngram, drafts are pre-computed from prompt history but the forward pass still speculatively evolves SSM state for all proposed tokens. **Key files involved:** - `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py` — `postprocess_mamba()` state copy logic - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py` — GDN metadata passes `num_accepted_tokens` but no state rollback - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — `_update_states_after_model_execute()` - `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/abstract.py` — `num_speculative_blocks` allocation ### Expected behavior Ngram speculative decoding should produce identical output to non-speculative decoding (with temperature=0, output should be deterministic and match). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [X] I have searched existing issues and confirmed this is not a duplicate - [X] I have verified the issue persists on the latest nightly build - [X] I have included reproduction steps and root cause analysis

items.title: [Bug]: ngram_gpu speculative decoding can propose draft tokens past max_model_len budget
items.body:
### Environment

Current `main` at commit `a8887c208f34c04c3b021cf3949ed6545d77bb01`.

Tested on a Google Cloud A100 VM:
- Driver: 580.126.20
- Python: 3.10.12
- vLLM: `0.20.2rc1.dev310+ga8887c208` from source/editable checkout
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0

`python -m vllm.collect_env` excerpt:

```text
==============================
        System Info
==============================
OS                           : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version                  : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0
Libc version                 : glibc-2.35

==============================
       PyTorch Info
==============================
PyTorch version              : 2.11.0+cu130
CUDA used to build PyTorch   : 13.0

==============================
      Python Environment
==============================
Python version               : 3.10.12 (main, Mar  3 2026, 11:56:32) [GCC 11.4.0]
Python platform              : Linux-6.8.0-1053-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.35

==============================
       CUDA / GPU Info
==============================
Is CUDA available            : True
GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
Nvidia driver version        : 580.126.20
cuDNN version                : 9.13.0 libraries present

==============================
         vLLM Info
==============================
vLLM Version                 : 0.20.2rc1.dev310+ga8887c208 (git sha: a8887c208)
vLLM Build Flags:
  CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled
```

### Bug

The V1 `ngram_gpu` speculative proposer can report valid draft tokens even when the target sequence has no remaining `max_model_len` budget.

The CPU n-gram proposer has an explicit cap:

```python
k = min(k, max_model_len - total_token)
if k <= 0:
    return np.empty((0,), dtype=origin_tokens.dtype)
```

The GPU path computes draft validity from the kernel output and `combined_mask`, but does not also clamp by:

```python
remaining = max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp
position < remaining
```

### Temporary instrumentation used

I added this immediately after the `self.kernel(...)` call in `NgramProposerGPU.propose`:

```python
remaining = (self.max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp).clamp(min=0, max=self.k)
bad = num_valid_draft_tokens > remaining
if bad.any().item():
    bad_rows = torch.nonzero(bad, as_tuple=False).flatten()
    dump_rows = []
    for row_tensor in bad_rows[:8]:
        row = int(row_tensor.item())
        nt = int(num_tokens_tmp[row].item())
        tail_start = max(0, nt - 32)
        dump_rows.append({
            "batch_row": row,
            "num_tokens_no_spec": int(num_tokens_no_spec[row].item()),
            "valid_sampled_tokens_count": int(valid_sampled_tokens_count[row].item()),
            "num_tokens_tmp": nt,
            "remaining": int(remaining[row].item()),
            "draft_tokens": draft_tokens[row].detach().cpu().tolist(),
            "num_valid_draft_tokens": int(num_valid_draft_tokens[row].item()),
            "token_ids_tail": token_ids_gpu[row, tail_start:nt].detach().cpu().tolist(),
            "max_model_len": self.max_model_len,
            "k": self.k,
        })
    print("NGRAM_GPU_MAX_MODEL_LEN_VIOLATION", dump_rows, flush=True)
    raise RuntimeError(
        "ngram_gpu proposed more draft tokens than remaining max_model_len budget"
    )
```

I also logged the upstream drafter guard around `input_fits_in_drafter` in `GPUModelRunner`.

### Minimal repro script

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

spec = {
    "method": "ngram_gpu",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 1,
    "prompt_lookup_min": 2,
    "prompt_lookup_max": 5,
}

llm = LLM(
    model="facebook/opt-125m",
    max_model_len=17,
    enforce_eager=True,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
    speculative_config=spec,
    seed=1234,
)

prompt = "def f(x):\n    return x + 1\n\n"  # 15 OPT tokens
params = SamplingParams(
    temperature=0.0,
    max_tokens=64,
    ignore_eos=True,
    seed=1234,
)

out = llm.generate([prompt], params)
print(out[0].outputs[0].text)
```

### Observed output with instrumentation

```text
NGRAM_GPU_DRAFTER_GUARD max_seq_len=15 num_spec_tokens=1 effective_drafter_max_model_len=17 input_fits_in_drafter=True
NGRAM_GPU_DRAFTER_GUARD max_seq_len=16 num_spec_tokens=1 effective_drafter_max_model_len=17 input_fits_in_drafter=True
NGRAM_GPU_MAX_MODEL_LEN_VIOLATION [{'batch_row': 0, 'num_tokens_no_spec': 16, 'valid_sampled_tokens_count': 1, 'num_tokens_tmp': 17, 'remaining': 0, 'draft_tokens': [1437], 'num_valid_draft_tokens': 1, 'token_ids_tail': [2, 9232, 856, 1640, 1178, 3256, 50118, 1437, 1437, 1437, 671, 3023, 2055, 112, 50140, 1437, 1437], 'max_model_len': 17, 'k': 1}]
RuntimeError: ngram_gpu proposed more draft tokens than remaining max_model_len budget
```

This shows `num_tokens_tmp == max_model_len == 17`, `remaining == 0`, but `num_valid_draft_tokens == 1` and `draft_tokens == [1437]`.

### CPU ngram and no-spec comparison

Same prompt, same model, same `max_model_len=17`, same `num_speculative_tokens=1`, only changing the speculative method:

```text
method: ngram
PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS 15
OUTPUT_TOKEN_IDS 2
FINISH_REASON length
TEXT_HEAD '  '
```

No speculative decoding:

```text
method: none
PROMPT_TOKEN_IDS 15
OUTPUT_TOKEN_IDS 2
FINISH_REASON length
TEXT_HEAD '  '
```

Both stop cleanly at the context boundary. The invariant violation is specific to `ngram_gpu`.

### Additional note

With larger settings like `max_model_len=64`, prompt length 60, and `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `ngram_gpu` also reached a CUDA device-side assert in `Indexing.cu` after the upstream guard logged `input_fits_in_drafter=False`. The reduced `k=1` instrumentation above is the cleaner repro because it catches the leaf invariant directly before that asynchronous CUDA failure path.

This is distinct from GDN/Mamba n-gram speculative issues: the repro uses `facebook/opt-125m` and V1 `method="ngram_gpu"` only.

### Expected behavior

`ngram_gpu` should never report more valid draft tokens than the remaining target `max_model_len` budget. It should match the CPU n-gram proposer behavior and return zero/capped draft tokens near the boundary.

### Possible fix direction

Clamp/mask by remaining budget in `NgramProposerGPU.propose` or `NgramGPUKernel.forward`, for example:

```python
remaining = (self.max_model_len - num_tokens_tmp).clamp(min=0, max=self.k)
combined_mask &= remaining > 0
draft_tokens = torch.where(
    torch.arange(self.k, device=device).unsqueeze(0) < remaining.unsqueeze(1),
    draft_tokens,
    torch.full_like(draft_tokens, -1),
)
num_valid_draft_tokens = torch.minimum(num_valid_draft_tokens, remaining)
```

A regression test should construct a repeated n-gram near `max_model_len` and assert GPU and CPU n-gram proposal lengths agree.

items.title: [Bug]: ngram speculative decoding default prompt_lookup_min=2 causes tool-call output corruption on Qwen3-class models with structured output (config-only fix: prompt_lookup_min=8)
items.body:
### Summary

When using `--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","prompt_lookup_min":2,...}'` (the default `prompt_lookup_min`) with a Qwen3-class model AND `tool_choice=auto` requests AND a tools array in the system prompt, **tool-call output is corrupted in ~50% of requests** even on a stack with all known related fixes applied (#40738 Phase 1+2, #36138, #40783, #39055).

The corruption manifests as wrong-token cascades like `<tool_call>\n<<tool_code>\nprint(...)`, `parameter=parameter=name`, `<<argname>...<argvalue>` instead of the correct chat-template format `<tool_call>\n<<function=NAME>\n<parameter=KEY>\nVALUE\n</parameter>...`.

**Config-only workaround (no code changes): set `prompt_lookup_min=8`. Achieves 100% clean tool-call rate (n=30 single-query, 96% n=25 multi-query) on the same hardware/model where default `prompt_lookup_min=2` gave ~50%.**

This is a separate bug class from PR #40738 (GDN state corruption, which we backported and confirmed gives +30-40% improvement). The remaining ~50% residual that the four upstream PRs don't close is the rejection-sampling artifact described here.

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.19.2rc1.dev205+g07351e088` (latest nightly tested)
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (hybrid linear-attention + MoE + full-attention layers)
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA RTX A5000 (Ampere SM 8.6), TP=2
- KV cache: `turboquant_k8v4`
- Speculative config: `{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}` (defaults)
- Reasoning parser: `qwen3`
- Tool call parser: `qwen3_coder`
- `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`: `false`
- `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--enable-prefix-caching`

### Reproducer

```python
import json
import requests

PROMPT = {
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Get weather for Tokyo"}],
    "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_weather",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "city": {"type": "string"},
                    "unit": {"type": "string"},
                },
            },
        },
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "max_tokens": 150,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False},
}

# Run 30 times, count clean (parsed JSON without `<<` or `parameter=` artifacts)
clean = 0
for _ in range(30):
    r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=PROMPT).json()
    tc = r["choices"][0]["message"]["tool_calls"]
    args = tc[0]["function"]["arguments"] if tc else ""
    if "<<" not in args and "parameter=" not in args and args.startswith("{"):
        clean += 1
print(f"clean: {clean}/30")
```

Expected with default `prompt_lookup_min=2`: ~15-16 clean (50-53%).
Expected with `prompt_lookup_min=8`: 30 clean (100%).

### How we found it (investigation methodology)

This bug was located after backporting four existing upstream PRs failed to fully close the corruption rate. The investigation timeline:

1. **First hypothesis**: TurboQuant KV cache + cudagraph capture/replay (per noonghunna's six-probe ladder at #40807 / #40831). Disproved by Probe 6 (`cudagraph_mode=NONE` works) and Probe 9 (kernel determinism via bit-equality test).

2. **Second pass**: backported #40768 (z1ying, async-scheduler placeholder fix). No measurable improvement — vLLM auto-disables async_scheduling for ngram method (vllm.py:815) so the buggy code path doesn't execute on our config.

3. **Third pass**: backported #39055 (ZenoAFfectionate, Qwen3 reasoning embedded tool_call). +20% improvement (20% → 40%) — confirmed parser-level fixes were on the right track.

4. **Fourth pass**: backported #40738 (tdoublep, GDN+ngram SSM/conv state corruption). +30-40% improvement (43-70% clean). This is the largest single fix and addresses the GDN state corruption originally reported by @bhaktatejas922 in #39273.

5. **Fifth pass**: backported #36138 (sfbemerk, structured-output spec-decode reasoning-end timing) and #40783 (ExtReMLapin, Qwen3 multi-tool first-occurrence + streaming overlap guard). Combined +3-6% additional improvement (53-56% clean). Both are correct fixes for their respective bug classes; just not our dominant residual.

6. **Token-level tracing pass** (where this bug was discovered): ran the reproducer with `return_token_ids: true` + `logprobs: true`, captured 30 responses, decoded raw token IDs via the Qwen3 tokenizer.

#### What the token traces showed

CLEAN response — parsed as `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "Celsius"}`:

```
[ 0] 248058 = '<tool_call>'
[ 1]    198 = '\n'
[ 2]     27 = '<'    ← FIRST `<`
[ 3]     27 = '<'    ← SECOND `<` (the qwen3_coder template uses `<<function=>`)
[ 4]   1628 = 'function'   ← CORRECT word
[ 5]  27362 = '=get'
[ 6]  67017 = '_weather'
...
```

BROKEN response — parsed as `<tool_call>\n<<tool_code>\nprint(get_weather(city='Tokyo'))`:

```
[ 0] 248058 = '<tool_call>'
[ 1]    198 = '\n'
[ 2]     27 = '<'
[ 3]     27 = '<'    ← also two `<` (correct per template)
[ 4]  13766 = 'tool'   ← WRONG token here. Should be 'function' (1628)
[ 5]   4000 = '_code'
[ 6]     29 = '>'
[ 7]    198 = '\n'
[ 8]   1302 = 'print'   ← Python code follows because of wrong [4] token
```

**The model picks the wrong token at exactly position [4]** in the broken cases. Position [4] follows the `[27, 27]` `<<` prefix, and the wrong token is one of: `tool` (token 13766, from the `<tool_call>` system-prompt definition), `parameter` (15704), `argname`, `argkey`, etc.

### Root cause analysis

The chat template defines the tool-call format using XML markers that include `<<function=`, `<parameter=`, `</parameter>`, `</function>`. These tokens appear MULTIPLE TIMES in the system prompt's tool definitions section.

When ngram with `prompt_lookup_min=2` is asked "what comes after `[27, 27]` (two `<`)?", the algorithm searches for any 2-token suffix match in the entire context. It finds matches in:

1. The actual `<<function=...>` template definition (correct match — would draft `function`)
2. The `<tool_call>` opening tag (matches `[27, ...]` partially → can draft `tool`)
3. Any literal `<<` markers in user content
4. Multi-tool definitions (each with its own `<<function=NAME>` line)

The KMP-style longest-prefix-suffix matching in [`vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py) returns ONE of these matches (the longest, but ties are broken by position) and drafts the next k tokens from there.

The rejection sampler then verifies each drafted token against the target model's logits. For the `function` vs `tool` decision at position [4], the target model has `function` at probability ~0.7 and `tool` at probability ~0.2 (both are valid template-context tokens). The rejection sampler accepts a draft token when `target_prob / draft_prob >= random()`. Since ngram doesn't provide draft probabilities, the comparison effectively reduces to "is target_prob above some threshold". For per-token accept rate ≈ 0.8, the structural ceiling for clean rate becomes:

```
clean_rate ≈ (per_token_accept_rate)^num_speculative_tokens
0.8^3 ≈ 0.51 ← matches our 53% empirical measurement with default config
0.8^1 = 0.80 ← matches our 65% with num_spec=1 (statistical variance)
```

#### Why `prompt_lookup_min=8` fixes it

Setting `prompt_lookup_min=8` requires ngram to find an **8-token** suffix match before drafting. For tool-call output, the 8-token suffix `[27, 27, 1628, 27362, 67017, 29, 198, 27]` (`<<function=get_weather>\n<`) is unique enough that it almost never matches spurious system-prompt fragments — it only matches the FIRST tool definition (where the model is currently reproducing the template) OR doesn't match at all.

Result: ngram drafts almost nothing on tool-call requests, producing close to no-spec correctness. Natural-language repetitions (where 8+ token matches do occur, e.g. repeated phrases in long text) still get speculative speedup.

### Empirical proof (clean-rate progression)

All measurements on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, 2× A5000, vLLM dev205+g07351e088, with all four upstream backports (#40738 Phase 1+2, #36138, #40783, #39055) applied. n=20-30 reproducer runs per row.

| Config | Clean rate |
|---|---|
| `prompt_lookup_min=2` (default) | 53% (16/30) |
| `prompt_lookup_min=2`, `num_speculative_tokens=1` | 65% (13/20) |
| **`prompt_lookup_min=8`** (single-query reproducer) | **100% (30/30)** |
| **`prompt_lookup_min=8`** (multi-query reproducer, 5 different queries × 5 trials) | **96% (24/25)** |
| no spec-decode (reference) | 100% |

Latency for 300-token responses: ~1.0s with `prompt_lookup_min=8` vs ~0.9s with default. Tradeoff acceptable for tool-call workloads.

### Working production configuration

```bash
--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":10,"prompt_lookup_min":8}'
```

### Proposed upstream changes

#### Option A — change `prompt_lookup_min` default

Change the default value of `SpeculativeConfig.prompt_lookup_min` from `2` (current) to `4` or higher. Document that low values trade correctness for speedup on workloads where the prompt contains repetitive XML/JSON template fragments (tool definitions, structured output schemas, few-shot examples).

#### Option B — add per-request opt-out

Add a `speculative_config_override` field to chat completion requests so callers can disable spec decoding for individual requests where correctness is paramount. Existing example: tool-call requests could set `enable_speculative=false` while general text requests keep speculative enabled.

#### Option C — context-aware ngram

Modify [`_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py) to skip matches that would land inside a structured-output template fragment (heuristic: prompt section identified by chat template markers). This is more invasive but addresses the root cause directly.

#### Option D — documentation

At minimum, document in [`docs/features/speculative_decoding.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/speculative_decoding.md) that `prompt_lookup_min=2` is unsuitable for tool-calling workloads and recommend `prompt_lookup_min=4-8` for those cases.

### What we still need

1. **Confirmation on other Qwen3 variants** — we tested only Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8. The same template format (`<<function=`) is used by Qwen3-Coder family, so the bug should reproduce there too. Independent confirmation welcomed.

2. **Confirmation on other tool-call parsers** — we tested only `qwen3_coder`. Hermes / Llama tool-call formats may have different vulnerable positions. Worth testing.

3. **Sweet-spot exploration** — we tested `prompt_lookup_min ∈ {2, 8}`. Values 4, 5, 6 may give better speed/correctness tradeoff. We picked 8 as obviously safe; 4-6 might be sufficient with similar speedup.

4. **Reasoning-on test** — we tested with `enable_thinking=false`. With `enable_thinking=true` the model emits `<think>...</think>` blocks where ngram has even MORE template fragments to match against. Likely worse without strict `prompt_lookup_min`.

5. **Default-change PR reception** — open question whether the maintainers prefer Option A (change default), B (per-request opt-out), C (context-aware ngram), or D (documentation only). Happy to write the actual PR for whichever option is preferred.

items.title: [Bug]: Prefill with prompt length == 1 + num_speculative_tokens misclassified as uniform decode → FULL spec-verify cudagraph skips GDN/hybrid recurrent-state write → deterministic garbage (any spec method incl. ngram; v0.25.1 & v0.26.0)
items.body:
### Summary

With speculative decoding enabled, a **prefill whose prompt tokenizes to exactly `1 + num_speculative_tokens` (K+1) tokens** is misclassified as a uniform spec-decode batch by `_is_uniform_decode` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, shape-only check) and dispatched through the captured **FULL spec-verify CUDA graph**. On models with recurrent state (GDN / Gated DeltaNet hybrids such as Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6; Mamba-family presumably likewise), that request's recurrent state is **silently never written**, and every subsequent step computes from a zero state → **deterministic garbage output** for that request.

PR #47123 already fixes this (same root cause, opened 2026-06-30, still open — this issue documents the bug it fixes and adds independent root-cause evidence; we are intentionally **not** opening a duplicate PR).

### Root cause (traced on v0.25.1 sources; line numbers close on current main)

1. `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` classifies by shape only: `max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len and num_tokens == num_reqs * (K+1)`. A prefill with a (K+1)-token prompt (or N equal-length such prompts batched) matches exactly. There is no check that the requests are actually decoding.
2. The batch is dispatched with `uniform_decode=True` → the cudagraph dispatcher replays the captured **FULL** spec-verify graph.
3. The GDN metadata builder (`gdn_attn.py`) built **prefill** metadata for this step (`num_prefills > 0`), so the spec persistent-buffer refresh block (gated on spec classification / `num_prefills == 0`) never runs.
4. The captured spec kernels therefore read **capture-time NULL(0) state indices** from the persistent buffers. The NULL guard in `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` (and the conv update equivalent) **skips the recurrent-state write entirely**.
5. The prompt's conv/SSM state is never created; the first verify (and all later steps) read zeros at the correct slots → wrong logits → deterministic garbage.

Instrumented capture-vs-replay probes confirmed each link: the affected prompt's prefill never executes the GDN prefill path (python-side skipped, replayed as the FULL graph); pre-verify state reads are all-zero at the correct slots on the affected server, byte-equal to the prefill's write on an unaffected control server.

### Trigger condition (measured, not theoretical)

Garbage occurs **iff** `prompt_tokens == K+1` for a raw completion (or N equal-length such prompts arriving together). Every one of 6 test prompts garbled at exactly `K = its_token_count − 1` and was clean at every other K ∈ [2,15]:

| prompt (Qwen3.6 tokenizer) | tokens | garbles at K | clean at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 请用中文写一句关于春天的话。 | 8 | 7 | all other K |
| 请用一句话描述大海。 | 5 | 4 | all other K |
| 写一段关于春天的话。 | 6 | 5 (empty output) | all other K |

Scope proven by controls (all official-image or clean-source runs, temp=0, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`):

- **Any spec method**: MTP and `method=ngram` (no draft head loaded at all) produce the same garbage — the defect is prefill-time dispatch, proposer-independent.
- **Any quantization**: reproduced with W4A16 and W8A8 checkpoints (dispatch code is quant-agnostic).
- **Both official images**: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1` **and** `v0.26.0` reproduce with the same checkpoint and prompt.
- **Batch-independent**: 2 concurrent 8-token prompts at K=7 (16 tokens, 2 reqs) garble identically; concurrency never changes per-request query length.
- **Dense models are immune**: Qwen3-8B (dense) + ngram K=7 with an exactly-8-token prompt is clean — the same mis-dispatch occurs, but spec-verify attention over a fresh sequence is mathematically identical to prefill attention; only recurrent-state models lose state.
- Chat-template traffic is effectively immune (template padding makes `prompt_tokens == K+1` unlikely), which is why this hides well in chat benchmarks and evals.

Note for reproducers: verify the token count against the served model's own tokenizer — the same string tokenizes differently across models (e.g. the trigger above is 8 tokens with the Qwen3.6 tokenizer, 9 with Qwen3-8B's unless the trailing 。 is dropped).

### Minimal reproduction

```bash
vllm serve <any GDN-hybrid model, e.g. Qwen3.6-27B / Qwen3-Next> \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":7,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'
# no draft head needed with ngram

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "<model>",
  "prompt": "<any prompt that tokenizes to exactly 8 tokens>",
  "max_tokens": 32, "temperature": 0}'
# → deterministic garbage; the same prompt with one token more/fewer is clean
```

### Workarounds

- `--cudagraph-mode PIECEWISE` (GDN runs eagerly with correct prefill metadata) — verified clean across all repro configs.
- `--enforce-eager`.

### Fix

PR #47123 addresses exactly this (hybrid-gated `force_uniform_decode=False` when the batch contains context requests) and has unit tests. We independently validated an equivalent minimal guard on a v0.25.1 fork — in `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding`, when `force_uniform_decode is None`:

```python
if uniform_decode:
    uniform_decode = bool(
        (input_batch.num_computed_tokens_cpu[:num_reqs]
         >= input_batch.num_prompt_tokens[:num_reqs]).all()
    )
```

(zero-sync numpy views; capture paths pass `force_uniform_decode` and are untouched; also covers the analogous non-spec `q=1` shape collision of a 1-token prompt, cf. #39928/#39945). Post-fix validation: all previously-garbage configs clean; the (K+1)-token prefill dispatches `PIECEWISE, uniform=False`; genuine verify decode still dispatches its FULL uniform graphs; acceptance length (3.78) and decode throughput unchanged.

Happy to share instrumentation logs (dispatch descriptors, capture-vs-replay state checksums) if useful.

### Environment

2× RTX 3090 (SM86), TP=2, CUDA 12.x; reproduced on official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1` and `v0.26.0` images and on a v0.25.1 source build; GDN-hybrid Qwen3.6-27B (W4A16) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (W8A8) targets.

---

AI-assisted: Yes (Claude). Not duplicating an existing issue (none references this bug or PR #47123); intentionally not opening a duplicate PR since #47123 already fixes the same root cause.

items.title: GDN attention backend crashes with ngram speculative decoding on mixed decode batches
items.body:
## Description

The GDN (Gated Delta Network) attention backend in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py` crashes with an `AssertionError` when ngram speculative decoding produces a batch containing both regular decode tokens and speculative decode tokens.

## Environment

- vLLM version: `0.17.2.dev0+g95c0f928c.d20260313` (nightly)
- GPU: NVIDIA GH200 480GB
- Model: Qwen3.5 9B (uses GDN linear attention)
- Config: FP8 online quantization, ngram speculative decoding (128 tokens, prompt lookup)

## Error

```
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py", line 310, in build
    assert not (num_decodes > 0 and num_spec_decodes > 0), (
AssertionError: num_decodes: 1, num_spec_decodes: 1
```

## Root Cause

Line 310 in `gdn_attn.py`:
```python
# Function code counted on either presency non-spec decode or spec decode,
# but not both.
assert not (num_decodes > 0 and num_spec_decodes > 0), (
    f"num_decodes: {num_decodes}, num_spec_decodes: {num_spec_decodes}"
)
```

When ngram speculative decoding rejects some tokens, vLLM creates a batch with both:
- Regular decode tokens (from rejected/verified sequences)  
- Speculative decode tokens (new speculative proposals)

The GDN attention builder assumes these are mutually exclusive, but they're not when spec decoding has partial rejections.

The CUDA graph preparation code below the assertion also assumes mutual exclusivity — there are separate branches for `num_decodes == 0` (spec-only) and `num_spec_decodes == 0` (decode-only), with no handling for mixed batches.

## Behavior

- First 1-2 requests succeed (all spec tokens accepted → pure spec decode batches)
- Subsequent requests crash when a token rejection creates a mixed batch
- Engine dies permanently after the assertion failure

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B",  # Any Qwen3.5 model with GDN layers
    trust_remote_code=True,
    quantization="fp8",
    max_model_len=32768,
    speculative_config={
        "method": "ngram",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 128,
        "prompt_lookup_max": 12,
        "prompt_lookup_min": 2,
    },
)

# Run multiple requests — will crash after 1-2 succeed
for i in range(5):
    output = llm.generate("def hello():\n", SamplingParams(max_tokens=100))
```

## Impact

This effectively makes speculative decoding unusable with Qwen3.5 models (and any model using GDN attention layers), which is a significant performance regression — ngram spec decoding provides signifcant speedups

## Expected Behavior

The GDN attention builder should handle mixed batches where both `num_decodes > 0` and `num_spec_decodes > 0`, similar to how the standard attention backends handle this case.

items.title: [Bug]: TurboQuant KV × any speculative decoding (MTP or ngram) produces degenerate token loops — confirmed across dense and hybrid attention
items.body:
### Summary

When MTP speculative decoding is combined with any TurboQuant KV preset (`turboquant_3bit_nc`, `turboquant_4bit_nc`, `turboquant_k8v4`) on a Qwen3-Next hybrid model (DeltaNet + attention — here Qwen3.6-27B Lorbus int4-AutoRound), the model emits degenerate token loops on any workload that requires structured or exact output:

- **Tool-call prompts** loop: `<tool_call><tool_call><tool_call>...` emitted as plain text; `tool_calls[]` never populated.
- **Long-context recall** loops: needle-in-haystack retrieves the first token of the secret then loops (e.g. `"amber amber amber..."`, `"turqururur..."` at 10K–90K depths).
- **Streaming** occasionally loops: `"Wait, I I I I I..."` on open-ended generation.

Short narrative / code completions look fine, which is why initial benchmarks passed.

**Isolation:** MTP alone is fine (fp8_e5m2 KV + MTP → all tests pass). TurboQuant alone is fine (turboquant_3bit_nc, no spec-decode → all tests pass). Only the combination fails. Tested all three TurboQuant presets; all fail with MTP. MTP `num_speculative_tokens` 1 and 3 both fail. This is distinct from the CUDA-graph capture crash in #40807 (which is a prerequisite just to reach inference — the output-quality bug is observed on top of the CUDA-graph workaround).

### Isolation matrix

Qwen3.6-27B Lorbus int4-AutoRound, single RTX 3090, vLLM nightly `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:9bba4628a3b943e0dd33caefb94b811569ba1e97bdf23bee19a265c31b947ccb`, Genesis patches applied, `max_model_len=125000` for TurboQuant rows / `20000` for fp8 row:

| KV dtype            | Spec-decode | Tool calls | Long-ctx recall 10K–90K | Streaming         |
|---------------------|-------------|------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| turboquant_3bit_nc  | MTP n=3     | ✗ loops    | ✗ loops                 | occasional loops  |
| turboquant_4bit_nc  | MTP n=3     | ✗ loops    | ✗ loops                 | ✗                 |
| turboquant_k8v4     | MTP n=3     | ✗ loops    | ✗ loops                 | ✗                 |
| turboquant_3bit_nc  | MTP n=1     | ✗ loops    | —                       | —                 |
| **turboquant_3bit_nc** | **none**  | **✓**      | **✓ (all depths)**      | **✓**             |
| fp8_e5m2            | MTP n=3     | ✓          | ✓                       | ✓                 |

Row 5 (**TurboQuant alone, no spec-decode**) is the new data — full `scripts/verify-full.sh` run logged below.

### Hypothesis

The MTP draft head runs its own attention over the live KV cache. When KV entries are stored through TurboQuant (rotate → quantize → pack), the draft-head's attention distribution collapses on rare-token / structured-token contexts. Both the draft step and the verify step read the same TurboQuant-dequanted cache, so the noisy distribution matches across draft+verify and looping drafts get silently accepted.

Short / common-token generations are unaffected because the distribution doesn't collapse there — consistent with the PR #38479 benchmarks (which measured throughput + GSM8K + NIAH on `Qwen3-4B`, a non-hybrid non-spec-dec model) showing no quality regression.

### Repro

Minimal compose in our companion repo: https://github.com/noonghunna/qwen36-27b-single-3090/blob/main/compose/docker-compose.longctx-experimental.yml

Run `scripts/verify-full.sh` against it — tool-call (step 4) and long-ctx-recall (step 7) fail with degenerate loops.

**Two independent fixes confirmed:**
1. Switch `--kv-cache-dtype` from `turboquant_3bit_nc` to `fp8_e5m2` → every test passes (`docker-compose.yml` in the same repo, our current shipped default).
2. Keep `turboquant_3bit_nc`, **remove** the `--speculative-config` block → every test passes, confirmed today (TPS drops from ~85 to ~40 on the 800-word essay bench, but correctness is restored across all 7 verify-full.sh tests).

### Probe 1 log (turboquant_3bit_nc, no spec-decode)

```
[1/7] Server reachable on /v1/models ...                                   ✓
[2/7] Genesis patches applied ...                                          ✓
[3/7] Basic completion — capital of France ...                             ✓ reply contains 'Paris'
[4/7] Tool calling ...                                                     ✓ tool_calls[] populated with get_weather
[5/7] Streaming (SSE) ...                                                  ✓ streamed 19 chunks, 75 chars
[6/7] Thinking / reasoning mode ...                                        ✓ reasoning 412 chars, content 3 chars
[7/7] Long-context needle (ladder: 10K / 30K / 60K / 90K) ...
     ✓  9820 tokens: recalled 'violet iguana 85'
     ✓ 29320 tokens: recalled 'crimson capybara 89'
     ✓ 58570 tokens: recalled 'sapphire platypus 61'
     ✓ 91070 tokens: recalled 'turquoise iguana 15'
  ✓ all long-ctx depths recalled secret correctly
All checks passed.
```

### Relation to tracking issue #40069

The TurboQuant follow-up tracker explicitly lists both `Hybrid attention models` and `Speculative decoding / Eagle` as unverified under "Feature compatibility". This issue is a concrete reproduction of that combination failing, with probe data narrowing the fault to the MTP × TurboQuant interaction (rather than either feature alone).

### Suggested follow-up probes (not yet run on our stack)

- **ngram spec-decode × TurboQuant on the same model**: if ngram also loops → any spec-decode × TurboQuant is broken (verify-path / store-path bug). If ngram works → specifically the MTP neural draft head's attention read against TurboQuant-dequanted KV is the bug. Happy to run this probe if it'd help — leave a comment.
- **MTP × TurboQuant on a non-hybrid model**: Qwen3-Next dense-only isn't broadly available below 80B; the DeepSeek-V3/R1 class of MTP-enabled dense models won't fit on our hardware. Anyone with Hopper-class VRAM could test this much faster than us.

### Environment

Identical to #40807 (Ubuntu 22.04, 2× RTX 3090 Ampere, driver 595.58.03, CUDA 12.9, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, vLLM image pinned to the digest above).

## Name of failing test

- `v1/e2e/test_spec_decode.py::test_ngram_and_suffix_correctness[speculative_config0]`

## Basic information

- [ ] Flaky test
- [ ] Can reproduce locally
- [ ] Caused by external libraries

**Affected jobs:** V1 e2e + engine
**Category:** test

## Describe the failing test

The test_ngram_and_suffix_correctness test with ngram method fails because the speculative decoding output matches the reference output only 54 out of 100 times (54%), which is below the required 66% accuracy threshold. The test compares outputs from a reference LLM and a speculative LLM using ngram decoding (prompt_lookup_max=5, prompt_lookup_min=3, num_speculative_tokens=3) on 100 test prompts. The low match rate indicates that ngram speculative decoding is producing different outputs than the baseline model more frequently than expected.

Hi

For the past day or so, I have been testing the performance gains of the n-gram model for speculation. I was benchmarking standard models such as `opt-125m` or `starcoder2-3b`. My use case is the standard code generation problem.
I have seen that regardless of the configuration, the inference of the sample model n-gram model is Pareto worse than the inference without the n-gram model, pretty much regardless of the contents of the `speculative_config`.

## My initial benchmarks

### Setup

```bash
model = "opt-125m"
tokenizer = "opt-125m"
engine_args = {gpu_memory_utilization = 0.90, tensor_parallel_size = 1}
sampling_params = {n = 1, temperature = 0.0, top_k = 1, logprobs = 1, spaces_between_special_tokens = false, max_tokens = 1024}
```

### Speculative Decoding
When running my benchmarks with:
`speculative_config = {speculative_model = "[ngram]", num_speculative_tokens = 5, ngram_prompt_lookup_max = 2}`

I see in the logs:

```bash
...

```

### Vanilla case (no SD)

```

I am a bit puzzled. Our n-gram model inference has:
-  has an acceptance rate of 70% (good)
-  but the efficiency 40% (quite low judging from the [code](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/995e3d1f41ddd3068664e8f7ff578e36df9c642d/vllm/spec_decode/metrics.py#L24))
- much lower prompt processing throughput vs. vanilla
- 4x lower generation throughput.

Reducing the `num_speculative_tokens` to e.g. 3 does improve efficiency to 60%, but also lowers the acceptance rate to 60%, leaving the effective generation throughput unchanged.

I was wondering whether I could isolate my issue. After all, the `ngram` model should, in my mind, be fairly close to "free lunch", especially for low values of `num_speculative_tokens`. So I wrote simple code to reproduce the problem.

## Bug: `--speculative-config` argument parsing fails with AttributeError

### Problem
When running `vllm serve (model) --speculative-config`, the command fails because the argument gets parsed differently than expected, causing it to be converted into a `SpeculativeConfig` object instead of remaining as a dictionary.

### Root Cause
The issue occurs in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` where `--speculative-config` is added through the VllmConfig argument group:

```python
vllm_kwargs = get_kwargs(VllmConfig)
vllm_group = parser.add_argument_group(
    title="VllmConfig",
    description=VllmConfig.__doc__,
)
vllm_group.add_argument("--speculative-config",
                        **vllm_kwargs["speculative_config"])
```

This causes the argument to be automatically parsed into a `SpeculativeConfig` object. However, downstream code expects it to be a dictionary and calls `.get()` on it, resulting in:

```
AttributeError: 'SpeculativeConfig' object has no attribute 'get'
```

This error occurs in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`, line 1458, in `is_v1_supported_oracle`:
```python
self.speculative_config.get("method") == "draft_model"
```

### Solution
Remove `--speculative-config` from the VllmConfig argument group and add it as a separate argument with proper JSON parsing:

```python
vllm_kwargs = get_kwargs(VllmConfig)
vllm_group = parser.add_argument_group(
    title="VllmConfig",
    description=VllmConfig.__doc__,
)
# vllm_group.add_argument("--speculative-config",
#                         **vllm_kwargs["speculative_config"])
vllm_group.add_argument("--kv-transfer-config",
                        **vllm_kwargs["kv_transfer_config"])
vllm_group.add_argument('--kv-events-config',
                        **vllm_kwargs["kv_events_config"])
vllm_group.add_argument("--compilation-config", "-O",
                        **vllm_kwargs["compilation_config"])
vllm_group.add_argument("--additional-config",
                        **vllm_kwargs["additional_config"])
# Other arguments
parser.add_argument("--speculative-config", type=json.loads)
```

This fix ensures `--speculative-config` remains as a dictionary, which is what the downstream code expects.

items.title: [Feature]: Evaluate multiple ngram speculations in speculative decoding
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

 During the ngram-spec-decode stage, I've always had a question: In RAG, there isn't just one document relevant to the answer; why don't we first let the large model generate 3 tokens, and then take all possible results in the N-gram?

In simpler terms, imagine you're looking for an object in several rooms but can only carry three things at once. You might want to pick up some important items now so you won't forget them when carrying more stuff later. This way, you make sure your search is efficient and effective.

items.title: [Speculative decoding] [Bugfix] Fix overallocation in ngram + spec logprobs
items.body:
There's a bug introduced in my spec logprobs PR that only shows up for ngram. We missed it because the ngram tests weren't actually running until recently (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/4551).

The bug is that the output logprob tensor of shape (batch_size, num_speculation, vocab_size, sizeof(float32)) is returned once per step, instead of slicing it into (batch_size, 1, vocab_size, sizeof(float32)) views. The spec decode framework does a torch.stack to make contiguous the logprobs of all steps; this caused quadratic memory allocation in num_steps. for a high enough batch size it can cause ooms (e.g. 64).

This is fixed by appropriately slicing the output logprobs.
